David did not shut the door in the face of the tribe of Benjamin because of the actions of King Saul, but won his son Jonathan to his side, and won many men of valour.
v Among those who oppose us most strongly are people appointed to be our friends.

St. Augustine v By loving a person who is your enemy you become a friend of God; in truth not only His friend but also His son, as the Lord Himself says: "Love your enemies... do good to them that hate you... [This proves that you are the sons of your Father in heaven]" (cf. Mt 5:44-45)[5].

Father Caesarius, Bishop of Arles v When he says "Be kindly affectioned one to another" (Rom 12:10), he means, be friends and be warm as well. Do not wait for others to love you, but leap toward them yourself and be the one who begins. By this you also reap the reward of their love. He showed why we must love one another and told us of the way in which steadfast affection is kindled, when he added, saying: "in honour preferring one another" (Rom 12:10). This is the way that produces affection, and in which affection dwells once it has been produced. Nothing creates friends like zealously striving to honour one's neighbor.
v It is no small effort; it requires an active soul and a great mind for us to endure separation from a person whom we love in Christ.

St. John Chrysostom Some think that what is mentioned here about the tribe of Benjamin [6-11] came by an error in copying, the word "Benjamin" being copied instead of "son of Zebulun," and in one of the Greek manuscripts "Zebulun" appears instead of Benjamin. Moreover, no mention of Zebulun has come in 1 Chronicles unless the text here is about him.

entries.section: 2. Benjamin the ravening wolf

paragraphs.text: Also, as stated in (Gen 49:13), Zebulun is situated on the seashore below Phoenicia; this fact seems to be reflected in the mention of Tharshish [10], which is the name of an ancient port (Cadiz), where ships came from the western side of the Mediterranean Sea (Spain)[6].
The sons of Benjamin; Bela, and Becher, and Jediael, three. [6]
Bela: a Hebrew name, meaning "swallowing or the ark".
Becher: a Hebrew name, meaning "the firstborn, that is, the first and the early one".
Jediael: a Hebrew name, meaning "known in God". He was a Benjamite and the head of a clan (1 Chr 7:6, 10, 11).

entries.section: 2. Benjamin the ravening wolf

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Bela; Ezbon, and Uzzi, and Uzziel, and Jerimoth, and Iri, five.
Heads of the house of their fathers, mighty men of valour; and were reckoned by their genealogies twenty and two thousand and thirty and four. [7]
Ezbon: a Hebrew name; the meaning of this name is not known with certainty, and it is the name of a son of Bela son of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:7).
Jerimoth: a Hebrew name, meaning "swollen or huge or tall". Two bore this name, and they are:
A Benjamite, son of Bela (1 Chr 7:7).
A Benjamite, son of Becher (1 Chr 7:8).
Iri: a Hebrew name, meaning "watchman". He was a son of Bela, of the sons of Benjamin. He was also called Ir.

entries.section: 2. Benjamin the ravening wolf

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Becher; Zemira, and Joash, and Eliezer, and Elioenai, and Omri, and Jerimoth, and Abiah, and Anathoth, and Alameth.
All these are the sons of Becher. [8]
Zemira: a Hebrew name, meaning "a song, or an elegant beardless youth, or small in size," and he was a man of the descendants of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:8).
Joash: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has come to aid". He was the name of a son of Becher, and a head of a Benjamite clan in the days of David (1 Chr 7:8).
Eliezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "God is help". He was a chief of the sons of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:8).
Elioenai: a Hebrew name, meaning "my eyes are toward Jehovah". It is the name of a head of a house in the tribe of Benjamin.
Omri: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "prosperous". He was a son of Becher, of the sons of Benjamin.
Abiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "the Lord is father or the Lord is my father".
Anathoth: a Canaanite name, the plural of "Anath". He was the son of Becher the Benjamite and a head of a house in his tribe.
Alameth: a Hebrew name, meaning "concealment". He was a son of Becher of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:8).

entries.section: 2. Benjamin the ravening wolf

paragraphs.text: And the number of them, after their genealogy by their generations, heads of the house of their fathers, mighty men of valour, was twenty thousand and two hundred. [9]

They were careful to register their genealogies [9], besides their strong and constant attachment to the tribe of Judah. When the kingdom was split and they set up a separate kingdom, the tribe of Benjamin did not join them, but clung to Judah and never separated from it.
They point to those who cling to the Lion that came out of the tribe of Judah, our Lord Jesus Christ.

entries.section: 2. Benjamin the ravening wolf

paragraphs.text: And the son of Jediael; Bilhan: and the sons of Bilhan;
Jeush, and Benjamin, and Ehud, and Chenaanah, and Zethan, and Tharshish, and Ahishahar. [10]
Bilhan: it means "his night, or inexperienced". He is the name of a chief of Benjamin of the clan of Jediael (1 Chr 7:10).
Jeush: a Hebrew name, meaning "he helps". A head of a house of Benjamin in the days of David (1 Chr 7:10).
Benjamin: a Hebrew name, meaning "son of the right hand, or son of the right," and he was a chief (1 Chr 7:10).
Ehud: a Hebrew name, perhaps an abbreviation of the name Abihud, and he was a son of Bilhan of the tribe of Benjamin.
Chenaanah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "toward Canaan". He was a Benjamite, of the descendants of Jediael.
Zethan: a Hebrew name, meaning "olive tree," and he was a head of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:10).
Tharshish: a Phoenician name, meaning "a refinery". He was a man of the sons of Benjamin, son of Bilhan.
Ahishahar: it means "brother of the dawn or the daybreak". He was the son of Bilhan son of Jediael son of Benjamin.

entries.section: 2. Benjamin the ravening wolf

paragraphs.text: All these the sons of Jediael, by the heads of their fathers, mighty men of valour, were seventeen thousand and two hundred soldiers, fit to go out for war and battle. [11]

entries.section: 2. Benjamin the ravening wolf

paragraphs.text: Shuppim also, and Huppim, the children of Ir, and Hushim, the son of Aher. [12]
Shuppim or Shupham or Shephuphan: a Hebrew name, meaning "serpent". He was the son of a Benjamite, the head of the clan of the Shuphamites.
Huppim or Hupham: a Hebrew name, the meaning of which is not known, and he was a son, or a distant grandson, of Benjamin and the founder of a clan in that tribe (1 Chr 7:12, 15).

Hushim: a Hebrew name, meaning "haste, agitation". He was a Benjamite, a head of a clan, the son of Aher. Some think that it refers to the tribe of Dan, instead of what is said of him in (Gen 46:23) that he was the son of Dan[7].
Aher: a Hebrew name, meaning "another". It is the name of a Benjamite man (1 Chr 7:12).

entries.section: 3. Naphtali

paragraphs.text: The sons of Naphtali; Jahziel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah. [13]

Only the first generation of the fathers of this tribe is mentioned. None of their descendants is mentioned; perhaps the records of their sons were lost. His father Jacob likens him, in his love of freedom, to a hind let loose in an open wilderness and in the valley without obstacles, moving lightly and swiftly wherever she wishes. For he says of him: "Naphtali is a hind let loose (a female deer): he giveth goodly words" (Gen 49:21).

But this freedom was not an opportunity for dissoluteness and evil; rather, the tribe kept good relations with the rest of the tribes, offering "goodly words". And in the Book of Judges Deborah sang, saying: "Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field" (Judg 5:18), perhaps pointing to the extent of their striving in war. Moses the prophet blessed them before his death: "O Naphtali, satisfied with favour, and full with the blessing of the LORD: possess thou the west and the south" (Deut 33:23)... Thus Naphtali became a type of the gentle soul in its dealings with its brethren, enjoying the blessing of the Lord[8].

v We do not consider as free those who are free by their position, but those who are truly free in their life and nature... The freedom of the soul and its blessedness are the result of true purity and contempt for temporal things[9].
v The free man is he whom pleasures do not enslave, but who governs the body with good discernment and chastity, content with what God gives, however little, thanking Him with all his heart[10].

entries.section: 3. Naphtali

paragraphs.text: St. Anthony The following is observed in this tribe: 1. One of them married a Syrian or Aramean concubine [14]. 2. "Machir" came as the fruit of this marriage; and this son learned from his father's mistake and married a Benjamite girl [15].

Naphtali, the son of Bilhah: the book showed no interest in his genealogy [13]; his lineage is rarely mentioned, and the number of his fighting men is small. The list of Naphtali agrees with what is in (Gen 46:24); (Num 26:48).
Jahziel: a Hebrew name, meaning "God divides," and he was the firstborn of Naphtali (1 Chr 7:13).
Guni: a Hebrew name, meaning "anointed or light red". He was the founder of the clan of the Gunites.
Shallum: a Hebrew name, meaning "recompense". He is also called Shillem, which means "the Lord has made a recompense".
Jezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "he created, he purposed". He was one of the sons of Naphtali, and the head of a clan.
Bilhah: a Hebrew name, meaning "simple-minded or unwary".

entries.section: 4. Manasseh

paragraphs.text: 14 The sons of Manasseh; Ashriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bare; she bare Machir the father of Gilead. 15 And Machir took to wife the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, whose name was Maachah. And the name of his second son was Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters. 16 And Maachah the wife of Machir bare a son, and she called his name Peresh; and the name of his brother was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rakem. 17 And the son of Ulam; Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh. 18 And his sister Hammoleketh bare Ishod, and Abiezer, and Mahalah. 19 And the sons of Shemida were, Ahian, and Shechem, and Likhi, and Aniam.
The descendants of Manasseh who were east of the Jordan, in Gilead and Bashan, were spoken of earlier (1 Chr 5:23-24). Here the talk is of those who lived in Canaan, west of the Jordan.
Of the descendants of Manasseh was Zelophehad, who had no son, but all his offspring were daughters, so they claimed their right to the inheritance (Josh 17:3).
The sons of Manasseh; Ashriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bare.
She bare Machir the father of Gilead. [14]
The list of Manasseh includes both sides of the tribe, and points to the relationship with Syria.

It is clear that some Hebrew women also became wives of Syrian rulers. The list indicates that the half-tribe of Manasseh that was living on the east bank of the Jordan became something like a political extension of Syria, and suffered the same fate as Syria when the army of Tiglath-pileser appeared in 734 BC[11].

It is noted in these few verses [14-19] that the genealogies refer to women, because of the devastation that befell Israel in the period of the captivity. Thirteen women are mentioned here, among them the five daughters of Zelophehad [15].

Ashriel or Israel: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "God strives". He was a son of Gilead of the tribe of Manasseh, head of the house of the Israelites. Here his name appears in the Arabic as "Ashriel," but in the Hebrew it is "Israel".

entries.section: 4. Manasseh

paragraphs.text: And Machir took to wife the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, whose name was Maachah.
And the name of his second son was Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters. [15]
Machir: a Hebrew name, meaning "purchaser". It is the name of the firstborn of Manasseh, and his only son by an Aramean concubine.
Maachah: a Semitic name meaning "zalam". The name of a woman of the descendants of Benjamin who married Machir son of Manasseh.
Zelophehad: a Hebrew name, meaning "shadow against fear, that is, protection from fear".
Zelophehad was the son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh (Josh 17:3).

The daughters of Zelophehad have special importance, since they had no brother, and it was feared that the family name would be blotted out, so they claimed their father's inheritance before Moses and Eleazar the high priest and before the princes and all the congregation by the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and boldly asked that their father's name not be taken away because he had no son. And the Law came giving the right to daughters to inherit from their fathers as long as they had no brother to raise up his father's name (Num 27:1-11). It was judged that the females should inherit if there was no heir other than they among the males, on condition that they not marry outside their tribe, so that the inheritance would not pass to another tribe.
The daughters of Zelophehad are mentioned five times in the Bible (Num 26:33; 27:1-11; 36:3-12; Josh 17:3-6; 1 Chr 7:15).
Their names are: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah (Num 26:33).

These daughters acknowledged that their father, although he did not take part in the company of Korah, yet died in the wilderness in his own sin, and he died and had no sons (Num 27:3). Yet they wanted their father's name to remain.

As true daughters of Israel who value their genealogies, they asked Moses to bring their cause before the Lord, and indeed the Lord answered their petition because of their zeal. And He made of their petition a statute of judgment for the children of Israel.
In (Num 36) the whole tribe of Manasseh is seen interceding on their behalf.

So it is fitting for the believer to marry from his own tribe, that is, from the daughters of God, or for believing women to marry the sons of God, so that believers do not lose their heavenly inheritance.
Indeed they married their cousins, and they asked Joshua to receive his portion as the Lord commanded.
v Hear, O penitent, do not delay your return, for you gladden the Father and the inheritance that awaits you.
The Father does not wait for you to offer Him a petition, but only wants you to return so that He may receive you.
The petition does not pay the bond of your debt; mercies will come forth and receive you if you repent.
Supplication cannot wipe out your iniquity, but tenderness walks the road by itself without your asking.
What you lack is to remind yourself of your stumblings, and the mercies of the Father take the place of all these (things) and you are made perfect.
Behold, Baptism gives you the robe of glory, and behold, faith is the king's ring on your hand.
The fatted calf of life has been slain for you that you may delight spiritually; all these things are yours, and you alone refrain from returning[12].
St. Mar Jacob of Serugh

entries.section: 4. Manasseh

paragraphs.text: And Maachah the wife of Machir bare a son, and she called his name Peresh; and the name of his brother was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rakem. [16]
Peresh: a Hebrew name, meaning "separation, distinction, dung". He was a son of Machir son of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:16).
Sheresh: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "root or shoot". In the family of Machir, of the line of Manasseh.
Ulam: a Hebrew name, meaning "first". He was a son of Peresh of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:16-17).
Rakem: a Hebrew name, meaning "embroidering, shaping, colouring". He was a man of the descendants of Manasseh.

entries.section: 4. Manasseh

paragraphs.text: And the son of Ulam; Bedan.
These were the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh. [17]
Bedan: perhaps he is the same Bedan referred to as one of the deliverers of Israel (1 Sam 12:11).

entries.section: 4. Manasseh

paragraphs.text: And his sister Hammoleketh bare Ishod, and Abiezer, and Mahalah. [18]

Hammoleketh: a Hebrew name, meaning "the queen". She was the sister of Gilead, and the daughter of Machir son of Manasseh, and she was the mother of Ishod, Abiezer and Mahalah [this is (1 Chr 7:17-18)]. Her sons had importance in the history of the Hebrews.
Ishod: a Hebrew name, meaning "man of splendour". He was a man of the tribe of Manasseh, and his mother was Hammoleketh.

Abiezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "father of help or father of aid or the father is help". He was the father of a clan of importance, from which came Gideon the judge who delivered Israel from the Midianites (Judg 6-8).
Mahalah: a Hebrew name, meaning "sickness". It is the name of a man of the tribe of Manasseh, the son of the sister of Gilead.

entries.section: 4. Manasseh

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Shemida were, Ahian, and Shechem, and Likhi, and Aniam. [19]
Shemida: a Hebrew name, meaning "the name will know". Of Manasseh. A head of the clan of the Shemidaites.
Ahian: a Hebrew name, meaning "my brother or a little brother". A man of the tribe of Manasseh of the clan of Shemida.
Shechem: a Hebrew name, meaning "shoulder, or the point of the shoulder". He is the son of Shemida, a man of Manasseh.
Likhi: of the descendants of Manasseh and the family of Shemida (1 Chr 7:19).
Aniam: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "I am an uncle, or a lament of the people". A son of Shemida of Manasseh.

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: 20 And the sons of Ephraim; Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eladah his son, and Tahath his son, 21 And Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath that were born in that land slew, because they came down to take away their cattle. 22 And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him. 23 And when he went in to his wife, she conceived, and bare a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it went evil with his house. 24 And his daughter was Sherah, who built Beth-horon the nether, and the upper, and Uzzen-sherah. 25 And Rephah was his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, and Tahan his son, 26 Laadan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son, 27 Non his son, Jehoshuah his son. 28 And their possessions and habitations were, Beth-el and the towns thereof, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer, with the towns thereof; Shechem also and the towns thereof, unto Gaza and the towns thereof: 29 And by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Beth-shean and her towns, Taanach and her towns, Megiddo and her towns, Dor and her towns. In these dwelt the children of Joseph the son of Israel.

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: We read of great things for the tribe of Ephraim when it reached maturity. Through the genealogies of Ephraim the writer brought out the position of Joshua son of Nun [27], who was the most prominent person in this huge tribe and was a type of the person of Jesus Christ in many respects [20-29]. In this section we find the only woman of whom the Bible says that she built a city [24][13].
And the sons of Ephraim; Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eladah his son, and Tahath his son [20]
Shuthelah: two bore this name, and they are: 1. A son of Ephraim, and the founder of the clan of the Shuthalhites (1 Chr 7:20). 2. Another of the descendants of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:21).

Bered: when the clouds suddenly pass into a very cold current, their pieces turn into frozen ice. Sometimes hail is a drizzle, because freezing overtakes the droplets of water falling as rain. And sometimes the pieces grow large, harming man, animals and crops.
Tahath: a Hebrew name, meaning "what is beneath". Two bore this name, and they are:
An Ephraimite, the son of Bered, of the clan of Shuthelah (1 Chr 7:20).
The son of Eladah, of the descendants of Tahath son of Bered (1 Chr 7:20).
Eladah: a Hebrew name, meaning "whom God has adorned". He was the son of Tahath of the tribe of Ephraim.

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: And Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath that were born in that land slew, because they came down to take away their cattle. [21]

The Bible does not refer to this event elsewhere, and opinions differ concerning it; we mention the following: 1. Some think that this event took place at the beginning of the tribe of Ephraim in Egypt, and that what happened was in the days of Ephraim himself, the son of Joseph. Others think that Ephraim here means another person of the same tribe, and that those who were killed were descendants of Ephraim, and not his direct sons. 2. Who were those who began the aggression against the other side? Some think that the sons of Ephraim thought that the time had come for the fulfilment of the divine promise, so they went down to Gath and plundered them in order to possess Canaan. And God allowed the men of Gath to kill them, because they moved rashly, in haste, and did not consult the Lord, nor wait for the time appointed by Him. Therefore the men of Gath executed judgment on them and killed them.

It is clear that the sons of Ephraim were shepherds of sheep in Goshen and had no military experience, so it is hard to imagine that they went down to Gath to plunder them. Rather, the people of Gath came to Egypt and killed the sons of Ephraim in order to drive away their cattle.
Later God gave the faithful men of Benjamin to drive out the inhabitants of Gath (1 Chr 8:13).

This tree of the tribe of Ephraim grew, and the divine promise on the lips of Jacob was fulfilled for them: "But his younger brother (Ephraim) shall be greater than he (than Manasseh), and his seed shall become a multitude of nations" (Gen 48:19).
Zabad: a Hebrew name, meaning "God has given, or a gift". He was an Ephraimite whom the men of Gath killed when he tried to steal their cattle (1 Chr 7:21).
Ezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "help". A son of Ephraim. He was killed in an attack on the Philistines.
Gath: a Hebrew name, meaning "winepress".
Most likely those whom the men of Gath killed were Ezer and Elead and their servants. And their father Ephraim mourned many days.

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him. [22]

Nothing grieves the heart of the aged father like the death of his sons, especially if the death comes by the shedding of their blood; therefore it is said: "And Ephraim their father mourned many days".

When the sons of Ephraim were killed, their father mourned many days and was not comforted, so his brethren came to comfort him, as Job's friends did when his sons and daughters died. Man's consolations are powerless and deficient, as Job said to his friends: "miserable comforters are ye all" (Job 16:2).

Most likely they comforted him with Jacob's blessing of him, when he laid his right hand on his head, and refused to move it to the head of Manasseh, the elder brother. He assured Joseph that his seed would become a multitude of nations (Gen 48:19).

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: And when he went in to his wife, she conceived, and bare a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it went evil with his house. [23]
God gave Ephraim a son, and although the birth of the son gave him some relative comfort, his affliction was very harsh, so he called the newborn Beriah.

Beriah: a Hebrew name, meaning[14] "in trouble or a gift". There are four persons in the Bible who bear this name. Moreover, in God's gift of a son to him, He did not give him on behalf of those whom he thought he had lost. No person takes the place of another, but each person has his unique personality, gifts and mission. Therefore when God restored to Job double what he had lost, He did not give him double the sons and daughters who had died, because they exist and are not lost!

Among the mistaken phrases that some often repeat in the case of the death of a son or daughter is: "May the Lord compensate you for him or for her." God compensates us for what we lose of possessions or honour, but those who have fallen asleep we do not lose, such that the Lord should compensate us for them with others.

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: And his daughter was Sherah, who built Beth-horon the nether, and the upper, and Uzzen-sherah. [24]

Beth-horon the upper: it is a Hebrew name, meaning "house of the cave". This name is given to two villages situated on the borders of Ephraim and Benjamin, twelve miles north of Jerusalem, and they were also called Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon. It is inferred from this that the one was built on high ground and the other on low ground.
Sherah: a Hebrew name, meaning "kinswoman". The daughter of Ephraim, who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sherah (1 Chr 7:24).

Uzzen-sherah: a Hebrew name, meaning "portion of Sherah". It is the name of a village built by Sherah, the daughter of a man in Ephraim whose name was also Ephraim (1 Chr 7:24). It is mentioned together with Lower and Upper Beth-horon. Its place is "Beit Sira", three miles southwest of Lower Beth-horon.

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: And Rephah was his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, and Tahan his son [25]
Rephah: a Hebrew name, meaning "wealth". He was a man of the descendants of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:25).
Resheph: a Hebrew name, meaning "flame". He was a man of the descendants of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:25).
Telah: a Hebrew name, meaning "a wound or a fracture". He was a man of the sons of Ephraim, probably from the line of Beriah (1 Chr 7:25).
Tahan: a Hebrew name, meaning "camp". He was a man of the sons of Ephraim and the founder of a tribe.

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: Laadan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son [26]
Laadan: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "fat of neck". It is the name of an Ephraimite, among the ancestors of Joshua.
Ammihud: a Hebrew name, meaning "my uncle is majestic". He was the father of Elisha, the grandfather of Joshua, a head of the sons of Ephraim in the wandering of the children of Israel (1 Chr 7:26).

Elishama: a Hebrew name, meaning "God has heard". He was the son of Ammihud, and one of the heads of Ephraim at the beginning of their journeying in the wilderness. He was one of the ancestors of Joshua (1 Chr 7:26).

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: Non his son, Jehoshuah his son. [27]
Nun: a Hebrew name, meaning "fish". He was of the sons of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:27).
Jehoshua or Joshua son of Nun: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is salvation". He was an eyewitness of God's work with Moses and Aaron during the plagues in Egypt and the exodus from it.

He was a disciple of Moses the prophet, his special assistant throughout the period of the wilderness. He took over the leadership after him (Josh 1:1). God is the One who raised him up as successor to Moses (Num 27:18-23). He brought the people into the Promised Land and drove out the pagans. He most likely points to Jesus Christ who alone opens for us the gates of heaven, brings us into the heavenly Canaan, and has given us the right of eternal inheritance.

Moses chose him with the rest of the spies who entered the Promised Land; he returned with Caleb son of Jephunneh, both of them instilling the spirit of hope in the people, unlike the rest of the spies who stirred up terror among the people.
He divided the Promised Land, and received his own portion after the tribes had received theirs, for the living, successful leader gives priority to others.
v Joshua son of Nun the righteous, who became a perfect disciple of the great Teacher (Moses), was also beautiful.
He also wanted love of life to triumph in him, and to draw near to God in perfection.
He kept purity while serving in the tabernacle of time (the tabernacle of the congregation), and became for the people a second Moses before God.
He fought to establish the word of the Lord among the peoples, and the mighty works he did made known how exalted his beauty was[15].
v Come and behold all the public beauty of Joshua son of Nun: the mighty deeds and great and astonishing works that were done.
When he cried out to the swift river and stopped its flowing, and its floods stood as though in an alley without flowing.
When he cleaved the river, and crossed as though on dry land, and led the forces behind him with great wonder (Josh 3:17).
When he fought against famous Jericho, and shouted with a voice at the high walls, and they fell before him (Josh 6:2).
When he prevailed over the kings of the Amorites, and the Lord arrayed Himself with him to destroy them (Josh 2:10).
When he commanded the height and it obeyed him, and sent him hailstones to stone the Canaanites (Josh 10:11).
When he commanded the sun, and it veiled its great power, and the moon heard his word and stopped in its course (Josh 10:13).
When he directed his voice to the galaxy, full of speed, and stopped it, and it stopped and the world ceased from its ordering[16].
St. Mar Jacob of Serugh

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: And their possessions and habitations were,
Beth-el and the towns thereof, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer, with the towns thereof; Shechem also and the towns thereof, unto Gaza and the towns thereof: [28]
Naaran: a town in Ephraim (1 Chr 7:28). It is called today Ain Duq. It is in the Jordan Valley, five miles north of Jericho.
Gezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "portion or dowry of the bride".
Gaza, which is not the Gaza known today in the far south and west, because the portion of Ephraim did not extend to the south, but rather the portion of Judah.

entries.section: 5. Ephraim

paragraphs.text: And by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Beth-shean and her towns, Taanach and her towns, Megiddo and her towns, Dor and her towns. In these dwelt the children of Joseph the son of Israel. [29]

Beth-shean: a Hebrew name, meaning "house of quiet". A city five miles to the west of the Jordan River. It first belonged to the tribe of Issachar, and was finally attached to the possessions of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:29). After the captivity it became the capital of the ten cities, and was called Scythopolis.

Taanach: a Canaanite name, meaning "sandy land". It was a city of the Canaanites mentioned around 1600 BC, when Thutmose III advanced against Megiddo. Its king was defeated and Joshua son of Nun slew him. It lies within the borders of Issachar, but was given to Manasseh (1 Chr 7:29).
Megiddo: a city of Manasseh, within the borders of Issachar, formerly a royal city of the Canaanites, which Joshua conquered with its towns (1 Chr 7:29).
Dor: a Canaanite name, meaning "dwelling".

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: 30 The sons of Asher; Imnah, and Isuah, and Ishuai, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. 31 And the sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel, who is the father of Birzavith. 32 And Heber begat Japhlet, and Shomer, and Hotham, and Shua their sister. 33 And the sons of Japhlet; Pasach, and Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the children of Japhlet. 34 And the sons of Shamer; Ahi, and Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram. 35 And the sons of his brother Helem; Zophah, and Imna, and Shelesh, and Amal. 36 The sons of Zophah; Suah, and Harnepher, and Shual, and Beri, and Imrah, 37 Bezer, and Hod, and Shamma, and Shilshah, and Ithran, and Beera. 38 And the sons of Jether; Jephunneh, and Pispah, and Ara. 39 And the sons of Ulla; Arah, and Haniel, and Rezia. 40 All these were the children of Asher, heads of their father's house, choice and mighty men of valour, chief of the princes. And the number throughout the genealogy of them that were apt to the war and to battle was twenty and six thousand men.

His father Jacob prophesied of him an abundance of good things, as Moses prophesied of him that he would "dip his foot in oil" (Deut 33:24), and both prophecies were fulfilled, for the tribe of Asher enjoyed a fertile land rich in olive trees from which oil is extracted. The yield of his land was plentiful, so it was said that his bread is fat, and he exported from it to the other tribes, besides his dwelling beside the sea, which enabled him to import goods and sell them to the rest of the tribes. This tribe points to the abundance of grace in the lives of the spiritual strugglers.
His portion, geographically, was in a location considered farther from Jerusalem than the rest of the tribes. The men of Asher, like Benjamin, were "mighty men of valour".
v May Your grace, O Lord, be the living Spirit, and the harpist who plays upon my strings, to bring forth a melody for Your sake, Your teaching[17].

v Grace has an eternal home, and she is a compassionate mother who cares for him, as a mother cares for her child, and she cannot leave him, because a woman does not leave her unborn child. And the child thinks that there is no other woman in the world but the one who nurses him. So the soul that loves God thinks of Him as its place... Wherever the true Christian is found, he dwells in God, and God dwells in him[18].

v Grace became a mother for the earth.. so she besought the Lord, saying: Enough of this madness for the earth! Come down and save it from error. The petition of grace entered before the divine Majesty, who sent the compassionate Physician to the sick[19].

v Grace - the mother of mercies - built the world, and she carries it; if she left it, it would fall. The hen spreads her wings over her chicks to gather them, to cherish them and to keep them. She sketches a type of the divinity that spread its mercies over the creatures like two wings, and protected them[20].
St. Mar Jacob of Serugh The sons of Asher; Imnah, and Isuah, and Ishuai, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. [30]
Imnah: a Hebrew name, meaning "good fortune, success". He was the firstborn of Asher and the head of a tribe (1 Chr 7:30).
Isuah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "equals". He was the second son of Asher (1 Chr 7:30).
Ishuai: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "equals". He was the third son of Asher (1 Chr 7:30).
Beriah: a Hebrew name, meaning "excellent".

Serah: a Hebrew name, meaning "one who explains". Serah is the daughter of Asher, and it was said that she was the only daughter, and it was also said that she was distinguished by her personality and beauty, and this was the reason her name is mentioned (1 Chr 7:30).

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel, who is the father of Birzavith. [31]
Heber: a Hebrew name, meaning "fellowship, partner".

entries.section: 1. The killing of the sons of Saul on Mount Gilboa

paragraphs.text: 1 Now the Philistines fought against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa. 2 And the Philistines followed hard after Saul, and after his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.

entries.section: 1. The killing of the sons of Saul on Mount Gilboa

paragraphs.text: After reviewing the genealogies, or the history of the children of Israel from creation to the Babylonian captivity (586 B.C.) in the preceding chapters, the writer returned to the period when the kingdom of Israel began. He did not begin with Saul’s receiving the kingship, but with his death, in order to bring us to the age of David, as the king whom God had chosen, who received a promise that his seed would reign forever. This was fulfilled by the coming of the King of kings, the Son of David, who reigns over our hearts eternally and raises up from His Church the Queen who sits at His right hand. Josephus, the Jewish historian, comments on what is said in this chapter [2], saying that since the writer opens his account of Saul the king with this battle, it is as though he wished to say that there was nothing good in the life of Saul worth mentioning on his behalf. He reigned for twenty years, as it were, without good fruit, and his life ended by his own hands, but with God’s permission, as though the Lord had killed him [14].

This period was one of the worst in the life of Israel, for the people insisted on appointing a king, which grieved the heart of Samuel the prophet (1 Sam 8:6). Although victories were achieved over some of the nations, the king sinned, and instead of repenting of his sins, what concerned him was his personal honor before the people. So his life ended with the people falling, together with their king, before the Philistines. It is as though the outcome of the people’s insistence on appointing a king like the other nations, and of Saul’s insistence on his own honor, was destruction for the king and the people!

Therefore it is fitting for us to seek the things that are above, and with our insight to pierce through earthly things [6].]

entries.section: 1. The killing of the sons of Saul on Mount Gilboa

paragraphs.text: And the Philistines followed hard after Saul, and after his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul. [2]
King Saul sinned, so disaster fell upon the people, and his sons also reaped the fruit of their father’s deeds.

Many are often astonished and ask: What fault is it of the people? And what crime have the sons committed? God allows this not in order to punish the people because of the sins of the leader, nor the sons because of the fathers, but in order to urge the people, as well as the sons, not to go astray after the errors of leaders and parents. This is what the Lord Christ affirms in saying: “He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me” (Mt 10:37).

entries.section: 2. The suicide of Saul on Mount Gilboa

paragraphs.text: 3 And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him, and he was wounded of the archers. 4 Then said Saul to his armourbearer, “Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me.” But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. So Saul took a sword, and fell upon it. 5 And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise on the sword, and died. 6 So Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house died together. 7 And when all the men of Israel that were in the valley saw that they fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, then they forsook their cities, and fled: and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him, and he was wounded of the archers. [3]

Saul abused the longsuffering of God, and thought that as a king possessing authority he was not subject to the law, and that there was no one to stand before him and call him to account. But divine justice overtook him and confronted him at the appropriate time, so his authority was taken from him, his family lost its dignity as a royal house, and David, the persecuted one, received the throne.

God forgives us all our sins.” To stop their mouths the wise man says: “Say not, His mercy is great; he will forgive the multitude of my sins” (Sir 5:6), and also: [As His mercy is great, so is His correction also] (Sir 16:12) [8].

paragraphs.text: v Now if the laws of men are observed with care, how much more is this required for the laws of God. A man says: “But He is good.” How long shall we utter this folly? I say folly, not because God is not good, but because he thinks of His goodness in order to achieve this end... Listen to the Holy Scripture, which says: “Say not, His mercy is great; he will forgive the multitude of my sins” (Sir 5:6). He did not command us to say: “His mercy is great.” He does not enjoin us this, but rather He wants us to say this always, and with the following purpose, which the Apostle Paul raises with every kind of proof. He means: Do not marvel at the compassions of God so that you sin and say: “His mercy removes the multitude of my sins”... but rather that we may not despair because of our sins, but repent, for “the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance” (Rom 2:4), not to a greater evil [9].

paragraphs.text: St. John Chrysostom v (The Lord) says through the mouth of the prophet: [My son, add not sin unto sin and say, The mercy of God is great] (Sir 5:5-6). “Not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance” (Rom 2:4). For who is as merciful as God, who forgives all the sins of those who return to Him, and makes the wild olive tree a partaker of the fatness of the olive tree; and likewise who is as strict as He, so that He breaks off the natural branches because of their unbelief? (Rom 11:17-24) [10].

St. Augustine More than once Saul aimed his spear at David to kill him, but the spear did not reach David, because the Lord preserved him for the purity of his heart. But as for King Saul, when one of the soldiers aimed his spear at him, he struck him at once with a serious wound, as though he drank from the cup that he had filled to give David to drink.

entries.section: 2. The suicide of Saul on Mount Gilboa

paragraphs.text: Then said Saul to his armourbearer,
“Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me.”
But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid.
So Saul took a sword, and fell upon it. [4]
Here we notice the following in the situation of the wounded Saul:

A. Saul realized that the more he strove with all his effort to obtain temporal honor, the more, when he fell into the hands of the Philistines, he would receive bitter insults. Thus those who hold honors, or who love great honors, are exposed to the danger of being exposed to scandal and mockery.
B. Whoever does not give glory to God in his success, the unbelievers can dominate him and make a public spectacle of his corpse.

C. Since Saul disobeyed the divine commandment more than once, even in the moments of his death he asked his armourbearer to draw his sword and kill him, so that the enemy would not mock him, but he did not listen to him; rather he disobeyed him.
